name: IRS21814STRPBF
title: IRS2181 / IRS21814: 600 V high- and low-side gate driver, 1.4 A / 1.8 A
summary: A two-channel gate driver for N-channel MOSFETs and IGBTs in a half bridge: one channel referred to ground, the other floating on a bootstrap supply whose return may sit at up to +600 V. Each output follows its own input in phase, with 3.3 V and 5 V logic accepted, no interlock and no deadtime, and the two channels' delays matched within 35 ns. VCC and VBS run from 10 V to 20 V, each with undervoltage lockout. The IRS2181 comes in 8-lead PDIP and SOIC; the IRS21814 adds a separate logic ground, VSS, in 14-lead PDIP and SOIC; IRS21814STRPbF is the 14-lead SOIC on tape and reel.

circuits.title: Typical connection, IRS2181
circuits.description: The 8-lead IRS2181 drives the two N-channel MOSFETs of one half bridge on a rail of up to 600 V. VCC powers the low side and, through the diode D1, tops up the bootstrap capacitor C2 between VB and VS each time the low MOSFET pulls the switch node to ground. Each output reaches its gate through a series resistor. C1 bypasses VCC to COM, C3 bypasses the high-voltage rail to the power ground, and COM, the low MOSFET's source and the rail capacitor share that ground. The switch node and the low MOSFET's drain each go out to the load.

circuits.title: Typical connection, IRS21814
circuits.description: The 14-lead IRS21814 drives one half bridge of N-channel MOSFETs on a rail of up to 600 V, its logic ground VSS kept apart from the power return COM. C1 bypasses VCC to VSS at the logic inputs and C3 bypasses VCC to COM. D1 charges the bootstrap capacitor C2, between VB and VS, from VCC. HO and LO drive the gates through series resistors; COM goes to the low MOSFET's source, where C4 returns the high-voltage rail. The switch node and the low MOSFET's drain each go out to the load.

operation.text: Two independent gate drivers for N-channel power MOSFETs or IGBTs: a low-side channel referred to COM and a floating high-side channel riding on VS, which may sit up to 600 V above COM. The high side is meant to run from a bootstrap supply. The output stages source 1.4 A and sink 1.8 A minimum (pulsed), with a reduced di/dt for noise immunity, and the buffer is built to keep cross-conduction inside the driver small.

HIN and LIN accept CMOS or LSTTL levels, 3.3 V and 5 V logic included (VIH 2.5 V min, VIL 0.8 V max over VCC = 10 V to 20 V). HO follows HIN and LO follows LIN, both in phase. The IRS2181/IRS21814 have no cross-conduction prevention and no deadtime; the IRS2183 and IRS2184 families add those.
The 14-lead IRS21814 has a separate logic ground pin, VSS, which may be offset by up to ±5 V from COM. On the 8-lead IRS2181 the logic shares COM.
VCC and VBS each have undervoltage lockout: rising threshold 8.0 V to 9.8 V (8.9 V typ), falling threshold 7.4 V to 9.0 V (8.2 V typ), hysteresis 0.3 V min, 0.7 V typ.

On the high side, HIN goes through an input level shift referred to VSS/COM into a pulse generator; a high-voltage level shifter lifts the pulses to the floating side, where a pulse filter sets and resets an RS latch that drives HO, gated by the VBS undervoltage detector. On the low side, LIN goes through its input level shift and a delay stage to LO, gated by the VCC undervoltage detector. Delay matching is 35 ns max.
The logic operates with VS anywhere from -5 V to +600 V. Between -5 V and -VBS the outputs hold their logic state. VS may slew at up to 50 V/ns.
VCC and VBS run from 10 V to 20 V. Each supply has an internal 20 V clamp, and all are tested at 25 V.

ton is measured from the input's 50 % point on its rising edge to the output's 10 % point, and tr from the output's 10 % to its 90 %. toff runs from the input's 50 % point on its falling edge to the output's 90 % point, and tf from 90 % down to 10 %. MT, the delay matching, is the gap between the HO and LO edges answering one input edge, taken at 10 % on turn-on and 90 % on turn-off. HO follows HIN and LO follows LIN, in phase.

The top face carries the part number (IRSxxxxx), a date code YWW followed by a marking code (P for a lead-free released part, blank for a non-lead-free one), the pin 1 dot, the IR logo, and a lot code whose first character is the assembly site code (per SCOP 200-002) followed by a 4-digit SPN code.
Qualified to the industrial level. The 8-lead and 14-lead SOIC packages are MSL2. RoHS compliant.
